hyperedges.label: macOS cross-build, bundle identity and install flow
Keeping MPE channels intact from plugin to instrument

nodes.label: build-macos CI job
nodes.rationale: There is no Mac in the development loop, so the macOS VST3/AU is cross-built on a macos-14 GitHub Actions runner. Manual trigger only (workflow_dispatch).

nodes.label: Ravel plugin target
nodes.rationale: Built in three formats (VST3, AU, Standalone). AU is left unconditional because JUCE's CMake filters it out on non-Apple platforms, so no if(APPLE) branch is needed.

nodes.label: RAVEL_BUILD_TESTS option
nodes.rationale: The engine takes PPQ positions as arguments rather than reading a playhead, so the sequencer core can be driven from a console app with no plugin host.

nodes.label: RavelProcessorTests console app
nodes.rationale: Drives the real processor through a mock playhead, covering the layer above the engine. JucePlugin_Name is normally a compile definition on the plugin target and has to be supplied by hand here.

nodes.label: RavelSnapshot editor-render target
nodes.rationale: Renders the editor straight to a PNG with no host and no visible window, so a layout change can be reviewed from a build step instead of by loading the VST3 into a DAW. Off unless RAVEL_SNAPSHOT_SOURCE is passed, because it builds a second copy of the editor.

nodes.label: RavelTests console app
nodes.rationale: Links juce_audio_basics, not audio_processors: SequencerEngine includes only ParameterTables.h, so needing audio_processors again would mean the plugin framework leaked back into the engine's header.

nodes.label: IAC Driver virtual port (macOS)
nodes.rationale: macOS ships loopMIDI's equivalent under a worse name and nothing needs installing - just tick 'Device is online' on Bus 1; from there the Windows steps are identical.

nodes.label: loopMIDI virtual port (Windows)
nodes.rationale: Free virtual MIDI cable; it has to be running for the port to exist, so it should start with Windows. Ports are enumerated when the plugin window opens, hence Rescan.

nodes.label: CC outputs (Mix CC and per-lane taps)
nodes.norm_label: cc outputs (mix cc and per-lane taps)
nodes.rationale: Two independent kinds: the Mix CC is the CC stack's fold, and each lane's own tap follows its raw step value and ignores Mix amount, since Mix amount governs the lane's share of the fold, not its own output. A column for a lane the instance does not have is greyed rather than removed, because all four lanes' parameters exist from load and a vanishing column would shuffle everything to its right.

nodes.label: Plugin-side MIDI port output (mirroring)
nodes.rationale: Ravel opens a system MIDI port from inside the plugin and writes notes, CC and bend to it with channels intact, so the messages never enter Live's MIDI graph. It mirrors rather than moves - the host still gets the same events - which is why the Ravel track's MIDI To must be left disconnected or every note arrives twice. Timing through the port is block-granular because the sample offset within the block is dropped.
nodes.source_location: MPE into Live: the virtual port route

nodes.label: Free Run
nodes.rationale: Keeps the sequencer moving while the transport is stopped so patterns can be auditioned. One shared switch for both stacks, because splitting it would mean running two independent timelines through the whole engine for a narrow benefit - the same shared-switch reasoning as Swing.
nodes.source_location: Quantize and continuous pitch / The tabs

nodes.label: Lane (16-step sequencer)
nodes.rationale: Each lane has its own length, rate, direction and mix amount; independent rates are where the polyrhythm comes from. All four lanes of both stacks exist as parameters from load because a VST3 cannot add parameters later, so lane counts only decide what is heard and shown - which is what makes them automatable and undoable.

nodes.label: MPE Lower Zone output
nodes.rationale: On by default: channel 1 master, 2-16 members, one member channel per sounding note. One channel has one pitch-bend register, so a channel each is what makes poly microtonality possible at all. The zone is re-announced with RPN 6 after a transport reset since a receiver's state cannot be assumed. A sixteenth simultaneous note steals the channel closest to finishing rather than exceeding the pool.

nodes.label: Pattern actions (RND, CLR, Invert, Rotate, Paste)
nodes.norm_label: pattern actions (rnd, clr, invert, rotate, paste)
nodes.rationale: They act on whichever row the lane's bars are showing, else they would appear to do nothing off the Value row, and across that row's own range rather than 0-1. CLR resets to each row's neutral rather than zeroing, because zeroing Velocity, Prob and Gate switches the lane off rather than clearing it. Rotate and Paste are the exception and move every row together, since rotating one row would slide it out from under the rest - Spread especially, because a window is measured from the pitch beneath it. All of it goes through the host as real parameter changes wrapped in gestures, and the logic lives in Parameters.cpp rather than button callbacks so it can be tested without a UI.

nodes.label: Polyphony (Voices and Poly mode)
nodes.rationale: In mixed mode polyphony is about overlapping gates, not chords, since pitch comes from the single mixed value. Poly mode gives each Note lane its own note, clock and block of voice slots so one lane cannot steal another's. A repeated pitch reuses its voice because MIDI cannot distinguish two identical note-ons on a channel - one note-off would silence both and the survivor would hang. Turning Voices down, or flipping Poly, releases anything outside the new limit rather than orphaning it.

nodes.label: Presets
nodes.rationale: .ravelpreset XML in Documents\Ravel\Presets, keyed by parameter ID with plain values so presets survive the plugin gaining parameters. Loading is an ordinary edit written through the parameters, so one Ctrl+Z takes it back and the host sees a real change rather than a state swap. A preset is only the patch - MIDI output device and window size describe your machine, not the sound.

nodes.label: Chance (per-step probability)
nodes.rationale: The roll is a hash of the timeline position rather than a draw from a running RNG, so it holds steady for the whole step and a loop skips exactly the same steps every time round instead of drifting.

nodes.label: Quantize and continuous pitch
nodes.rationale: Pitch always goes out as note plus pitch bend: the nearest semitone carries the note number and the residual goes out as bend, sent just before the note-on so the note starts in tune. With Quantize on and a 12-EDO scale the residual is exactly zero and no bend is sent. There is no glide - exactly one bend per note, and a Spread draw happens once as the step resolves.

nodes.label: Root and Range
nodes.rationale: Range counts in octaves rather than raw degrees so a given value covers the same musical distance whether the scale packs 5 degrees into an octave or 53. With Quantize on it maps onto degrees rather than semitones so every step lands on a usable note instead of several steps snapping onto the same pitch. Notes clamp to the MIDI range, so reachable range depends on Root.

nodes.label: Scales and EDO tunings
nodes.rationale: 12-, 19-, 23-, 31-, 41- and 53-EDO, each chosen for a different trade: 19 and 31 as meantones with near-just thirds, 41 for a fifth under half a cent from 3/2, 53 for 5-limit just and Pythagorean plus makam, 23 for mavila where the flat fifth turns the diatonic scale inside out. Every tuning keeps a 2:1 octave so patterns stay octave-aligned with the rest of the session. In-between degrees play as note plus bend, so microtonal work is limited to one microtone at a time per channel.

nodes.label: Slew
nodes.rationale: Smooths every CC the plugin sends, lane taps included, and never touches pitch - so it lives on the CC tab, filed under Mix CC as an ordinary fifth row because a rule and sub-heading to mark the distinction cost more attention than the distinction is worth.
nodes.source_location: The tabs / Quantize and continuous pitch

nodes.label: Spread (per-step pitch window)
nodes.rationale: Stored as a width rather than as the range's top end so it can be an ordinary row with RND/CLR/Invert - two endpoints would put Invert in the position of flipping floors past their own ceilings. Only the ceiling is clamped. The draw is a hash of the timeline position, not just for loop repeatability but because a lane is re-resolved every block whether or not it advanced, so a running RNG would redraw mid-step and zipper the pitch. It is applied before the lane's share is taken, so Mix amount scales the wander. Note-only because what it widens is a pitch; on a CC lane it would be step jitter, a different feature wearing this one's name.

nodes.label: Swing
nodes.rationale: Delays every other step of the absolute grid so it stays anchored to the bar rather than to where a short pattern started. One control across both stacks, because they fold off the same host clock and a Note lane swung against a CC lane reads as drift rather than groove. It moves step boundaries, so the index derivation picks the largest candidate whose shifted boundary has passed instead of floor(ppq/stepPpq); clamping the offset to +/-0.49 of a step keeps boundaries monotonic, and at zero swing it reduces exactly to the old floor().

nodes.label: The fold (mix += depth x value)
nodes.rationale: Lanes combine in lane order; both stacks fold the same way. A step toggled off, a lost Chance roll and a muted lane are all transparent for the fold, so those three states share one behaviour.

nodes.label: Absolute-PPQ timing derivation
nodes.rationale: globalIndex = floor(ppqPosition / stepLength) rather than an accumulated counter: in exchange for a division and a floor, loops, transport jumps, scrubbing and tempo changes land on exactly the step the timeline says, with no drift and no resync logic. Everything about a lane is a function of globalIndex, so it is resolved once per step boundary and the engine inverts the same inequality to find the next boundary's sample exactly.

nodes.label: Two stacks (Notes and CC)
nodes.rationale: Two separate sequencers sharing one clock, transport and plugin instance, each with its own lane count. They differ per step, not per lane: Velocity and Gate are arguments to starting a note and a CC lane never starts one, which also keeps the automatable parameter count from doubling for nothing.

nodes.label: Undo history
nodes.rationale: One edit is one turn of the message loop, so a forty-parameter pattern action is a single step. The plugin swallows Ctrl+Z either way rather than letting it fall through, since silently undoing the arrangement instead would be a far worse surprise. Host automation sends no gestures and never fills the history, which lives on the processor so it survives closing the window.

nodes.label: macOS install (VST3 and AU bundles)
nodes.rationale: Each format is only found in its own per-user folder. The mkdir lines matter because VST3/ is only created by whatever VST3 installer ran first, so on a Mac that has never had one the mv fails silently and it looks like a broken VST3.

nodes.label: Virtual port route for MPE (user-facing steps)
nodes.norm_label: virtual port route for mpe (user-facing steps)
nodes.rationale: Written for someone handed a build rather than a reader of the repo. Live's MPE input toggle is the step that matters - it is what makes Live read channels 2-16 as one zone - and the receiving track's channel selector must be All Channels or you are back to the collapsed case.

nodes.label: AU appears but VST3 does not - diagnostic list
nodes.norm_label: au appears but vst3 does not - diagnostic list
nodes.rationale: Ordered as questions with definite answers so the reader stops at the first wrong one: is the binary there, is it still quarantined, did the signature survive the unzip (some unarchivers rewrite metadata and break the seal), what did Live's log say, and is Live serving a cached scan failure (Alt+Rescan forces a full rescan).

nodes.label: Windows install (system or custom VST3 folder)
nodes.norm_label: windows install (system or custom vst3 folder)
nodes.rationale: Either the system folder every host already scans, or a personal folder pointed at via Live's VST3 Custom Folder. No quarantine equivalent; SmartScreen may warn because the build is unsigned.

nodes.label: build.ps1 development loop
nodes.rationale: Configures on first run and builds every run, and stops with its own message if CMake is off PATH or JUCE/ is missing rather than letting CMake fail further in. Drops the VST3 into Documents\VST3 so no elevation is needed. Live must be closed before rebuilding or the link step dies on a held DLL (LNK1104).

nodes.label: Editor PNG snapshot workflow
nodes.rationale: The editor is a juce::Component and can paint into an image without reaching a desktop window, so the whole window renders to a PNG from a build step - layout constants stay wrong by four pixels until someone looks. It dials in a fixed patch first because the defaults show none of the states worth checking, and animation frames need a Release build since a Debug paint costs more wall clock than the slide lasts.

nodes.label: EngineTests suite
nodes.rationale: 135 checks driving SequencerEngine over a synthetic timeline; possible at all because the engine takes PPQ positions as plain arguments rather than reading a playhead.

nodes.label: Building on macOS via CI
nodes.rationale: No Mac in the development loop, so the plugin is cross-built in Actions. The mkdir before mv is load-bearing: Components/ exists on essentially every Mac but VST3/ is only created by whichever VST3 installer ran first, so without it the AU installs, the VST3 silently does not, and it looks like a broken VST3. The build is ad-hoc signed only, so the quarantine flag has to be cleared with xattr.

nodes.label: package.ps1 and the Inno Setup installer
nodes.norm_label: package.ps1 and the inno setup installer
nodes.rationale: Handing the plugin to someone else is a different job from the dev loop - they want one file to double-click - so the installer elevates once and writes to the system VST3 folder, needing no custom-folder setup in Live. The version comes from the project() line in CMakeLists.txt so nothing under Installer\ keeps a second copy, while AppId is frozen for the life of the plugin for the same reason PLUGIN_CODE is. It is unsigned, so SmartScreen warns; and it checks for a Documents\VST3 copy left by a local build, which Live would otherwise list twice.

nodes.label: ProcessorTests suite
nodes.rationale: 145 checks driving RavelAudioProcessor::processBlock through a mock playhead - the layer where the plugin could compile, load and still emit nothing.

nodes.label: Ravel (polyrhythmic step sequencer)
nodes.rationale: Built as a VST3 instrument for Ableton Live 12 on Windows; silent by design because its output is MIDI, not audio.

nodes.label: Bundle artifact upload path convention
nodes.rationale: The path points at the bundle's parent folder, not the .vst3/.component itself: upload-artifact treats a given directory as the root, so pointing at the bundle would upload its Contents/ loose and drop the bundle name.

nodes.label: JUCE_TAG pin (9.0.1)
nodes.rationale: JUCE is not committed to the repo (.gitignore), so CI clones it. The tag is pinned to the same version the Windows build is developed against so a local build and a CI build are the same build.

nodes.label: Universal binary configure (arm64 + x86_64)
nodes.rationale: CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES="arm64;x86_64" with deployment target 11.0 so one artifact runs on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs; tests are switched off in CI.

nodes.label: EDITOR_WANTS_KEYBOARD_FOCUS
nodes.rationale: TRUE so the VST3 wrapper asks the host for keyboard focus; without it the editor never sees a keystroke and Ctrl+Z cannot fire.

nodes.label: IS_SYNTH + NEEDS_MIDI_OUTPUT plugin classification
nodes.rationale: Ableton Live does not host MIDI-effect plugins, but it does expose an instrument's MIDI output as a routing source on another track's 'MIDI From'. So Ravel ships as an instrument that emits MIDI rather than as a MIDI effect.

nodes.label: Per-format macOS CFBundleIdentifier patch
nodes.rationale: juce_add_plugin() derives one CFBundleIdentifier for every format, which Apple disallows once two are loaded into one process. JUCE exposes no per-format option, so the generated Info.plists are rewritten at configure time and XCODE_ATTRIBUTE_PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER is set too (Xcode takes the signing id from that, not from the plist). Only CFBundleIdentifier moves; the VST3 class ID and AU type/subtype are untouched so sessions still relink, and JucePlugin_CFBundleIdentifier is left alone because juce_CoreMidi_mac.mm seeds the virtual MIDI port's unique ID from it.

nodes.label: PLUGIN_CODE Trln (frozen 4-char code)
nodes.rationale: Kept unchanged through the rename because the code feeds the VST3 class ID; changing it would make existing Live sessions see a different plugin instead of relinking after a rescan.

nodes.label: RAVEL_VST3_DIR copy destination
nodes.rationale: JUCE's Windows default (C:/Program Files/Common Files/VST3) needs an elevated shell on every build, so builds drop into a user-writable Documents/VST3 and Live is pointed at it as a Custom VST3 Folder. USERPROFILE is Windows-only, so non-Windows falls back to HOME. The property must be set after add_subdirectory(JUCE) (JUCE overwrites the global while being processed) but before juce_add_plugin() (which bakes the destination into the post-build copy step).

nodes.label: Virtual-port caveats
nodes.rationale: Do not close the loop (feedback); timing is block-granular, under 3 ms at 128 samples / 48 kHz; the port choice is saved by name and falls back quietly to host output on a machine without it; one port per instance, because two instances allocate out of the same 15 member channels without knowing about each other and steal each other's notes.

nodes.label: Clearing the Gatekeeper quarantine flag
nodes.rationale: The build is ad-hoc signed with no Developer certificate or notarisation, so Gatekeeper refuses anything still flagged as downloaded and the plugin either fails its scan or never appears. xattr -cr must be run after the bundles are moved, since the paths are the final ones. This is the step people miss.

nodes.label: Bend Range and RPN transmission
nodes.rationale: Defaults to +/-48 because announcing an MPE zone makes an instrument's own bend-range setting stop applying and its members revert to the MPE default; a +/-2 default against a receiver reading +/-48 scales the residual 24x and flips sign every half semitone. With MPE off, RPN 0 is well supported and smaller means finer resolution. The RPN is written as raw controller events rather than via a JUCE helper that returns a MidiBuffer by value and would allocate on the audio thread, and closes with an explicit data entry LSB and a Null RPN - without the Null the parameter stays selected and every later CC 6 or CC 38 is swallowed as data, which on a plugin where any lane can be pointed at CC 6 would silently rewrite the instrument's bend range.

nodes.label: Step-boundary epsilon bug
nodes.rationale: ppqPerSample is 1/24000 at 120 bpm / 48 kHz and not exactly representable in binary, so floor(ppq/stepLength) returned the previous step and step lengths alternated between 5999 and 6001 samples. Fixed with an epsilon in SequencerEngine::process sized ~1000x smaller than one sample's worth of PPQ, so it can only snap a value already inside rounding noise.

nodes.label: CC loopback for modulating Live parameters
nodes.norm_label: cc loopback for modulating live parameters
nodes.rationale: A VST3 cannot drive another Live device's knob - there is no such mechanism in the format - so the workaround is a MIDI CC loopback through a virtual port plus Ctrl+M mapping. It is 7-bit and control-rate; true full-resolution parameter modulation is a Max for Live job.

nodes.label: The three Offsets
nodes.rationale: The Mix CC's Offset adds and clamps at the top; a lane's Offset instead raises that tap's floor and scales the step into the headroom above it, because adding there would push every step above the Offset into the same clamped ceiling and flatten the top of the pattern. The Notes Offset transposes in whole octaves after Root, Range and scale have resolved, so a pattern keeps its shape instead of being squashed against the fold's clamp.

nodes.label: Position-hashed randomness
nodes.rationale: Random direction, Chance and Spread all hash the timeline position instead of drawing from a running RNG, so a loop replays the same random pattern every time round and a pure function of position gives the same answer however often it is asked.

nodes.label: One LaneComponent for both lane kinds
nodes.norm_label: one lanecomponent for both lane kinds
nodes.rationale: Both lane kinds are the same LaneComponent, told at construction which params::LaneKind it is, and the same goes for pattern actions and the engine's fold - which keeps the two stacks from being two copies of the same code with a Note/CC flag sprinkled through both.

nodes.label: Live's channel collapse (why the virtual port is needed)
nodes.norm_label: live's channel collapse (why the virtual port is needed)
nodes.rationale: Live discards the zone twice: track-to-track routing strips the channel so fifteen member channels arrive as one, and Live's own external MIDI output makes you pick a single channel. This is a limitation of Live's routing, not something the plugin can fix from inside.
nodes.source_location: MPE into Live: the virtual port route

nodes.label: Row-switch slide animation
nodes.rationale: Sixteen bars changing height at once reads as the grid being replaced; sliding over ~140 ms says the pattern stayed and you changed which row you are looking at. The same code runs for pattern actions because the slide reads its destination live rather than capturing it, and it only borrows the drawn height - the parameter is never touched, so nothing reaches the host or the undo history.

nodes.label: RavelFonts binary-data target
nodes.rationale: Archivo is compiled in rather than loaded from disk: a plugin cannot rely on the host machine having a font, and JUCE's default sans-serif differs per OS (Segoe UI vs Helvetica), which turns a layout measured against one font into overlapping text on the other. POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE is required because the plugin targets are shared libraries.

nodes.label: Embedded Archivo faces
nodes.rationale: Assets/*.ttf are compiled in by the RavelFonts target and created once and cached in Theme.cpp, so every string is measured and drawn in the same two faces on every platform.
